learning_outcomes.text: Describe the main laws of electromagnetism.
Explain the basic concepts about the general laws of electromagnetism and their application to solve engineering problems.
Demonstrate the handling of basic concepts about the general laws of electromagnetism to solve engineering-related problems.
Extract relevant information from an experimental setup to contrast results with theory.
Interpret available information on an engineering problem to obtain its solution.
Justify the appropriate physical parameters to implement an engineering project.

syllabus_topics: Electrostatic field. Field lines. Gauss's Law.
Capacitors. Energy stored in a capacitor.
Kirchhoff's Laws and DC circuit analysis.
Force exerted by a magnetic field.
Magnetic field created by electric currents: Biot-Savart Law.
Self-induction and mutual induction. Energy stored in an inductor.
DC circuits. Identification and measurement of resistances with a multimeter. Measurement of voltages and currents.
Basic measurements with an oscilloscope: voltage, frequency, and phase angles in AC currents.
Transformer: Measurement of voltage ratio between the primary and secondary of a transformer.
Group work on the physical fundamentals, development, results and conclusions of one of the practical activities, presented in English.
assessment_rules: The final grade (CF) in continuous evaluation is CF = 20%*C1 + 20%*C2 + 20%*PL + 40%*C3. A minimum grade of 5/10 is required in each activity (C1, C2, PL, C3); otherwise, the final grade is 'Fail' with the lowest numerical score. Mandatory attendance and a minimum grade of 5.0 on laboratory practicals (PL) are required, with an option for a second submission for PL reports to achieve a maximum of 5.0. For single evaluation, CF = 20%*PL + 80%*EF, requiring a minimum of 5/10 in both PL and EF. Passed grades for C1, C2, and PL can be conserved for resits.
